record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Among all positive realizations of a given transfer function that have minimal possible state dimension, what is the structure of the space of such realizations? More specifically, how are all positive minimal realizations connected to one another?

evidence.quote: The positive realization problem consists of providing answers to the questions: - (The minimality problem) What is a minimal value for N?
- how are all positive minimal realizations connected?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H(z)$ be a rational transfer function with non-negative impulse response (so that it admits positive realizations). A positive realization of $H(z)$ of dimension $N$ is a quadruple $(A,b,c,d)$ with $A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}$, $b\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, $c^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{N}$, $d\in\mathbb{R}$ such that all entries of $A$, $b$, $c$, $d$ are non-negative and
$$H(z)=c^{T}(zI-A)^{-1}b+d.$$
Let $N_{\min}(H)$ denote the smallest integer $N$ for which such a positive realization exists, and let $\mathcal{M}(H)$ denote the set of all positive realizations of $H(z)$ of dimension exactly $N_{\min}(H)$, considered up to permutation similarity (i.e., $(A,b,c,d)\sim(PAP^{T},Pb,Pc,d)$ for any permutation matrix $P$).

Describe the structure of $\mathcal{M}(H)$. In particular, determine whether $\mathcal{M}(H)$ is always connected (in a suitable natural topology, e.g., as a subset of Euclidean space modulo permutation equivalence), and more generally describe how any two minimal positive realizations of $H(z)$ can be transformed into one another.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (including a 2022 survey in Automatica and 2025 work on minimal positive Markov realizations) confirm that the characterization of minimality for positive realizations remains an open problem, and the structure/connectedness of the set of minimal positive realizations is not known in general. Progress exists only for special subclasses.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey - ScienceDirect (2022)
status_evidence.snippet: The characterization of minimality for positive systems is still an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of minimal positive realizations remains open as of 2022.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations (arXiv:2502.21102)
status_evidence.snippet: proposes a linear programming approach... minimum dimension of positive Markov realizations is an upper bound of the minimal positive realization dimension
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses only restricted subclasses, indicating the general problem is still open.
